subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared `notificationWake.reactions` policy as the canonical way to make Telegram reactions wake agents, or should Telegram reaction semantics be split into a narrower/different product surface?
rationale: The remaining work changes a user-facing control surface and config/API shape; source confirms the gap, but automation cannot choose the long-term reaction semantics contract for maintainers.

options.title: Adopt shared wake policy
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 or its successor as the canonical path for opt-in wake behavior and stable reaction keys across Telegram and sibling channels.

options.title: Split wake from semantics
options.body: Land only the narrow wake/key support now, and keep per-emoji meanings, prompt guidance, or durable feedback in separate issues such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/9835 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94963.

options.title: Reject core reaction execution
options.body: Keep Telegram reactions as passive context events and close or supersede the linked reaction-wake work with a clear product rationale.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared wake policy
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 or its successor as the canonical path for opt-in wake behavior and stable reaction keys across Telegram and sibling channels.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the currently open same-repo shared notification wake policy candidate and has adjacent Telegram channel assembly history.
